provenance: Curated by AI-assisted inspection of the elaborated statements and source proofs. These descriptions and tags aid search; the exact statements/dependencies are separately extracted from Lean in proof-index.json. No Prove2Me/Formalpedia upload or external human review is asserted.

QuantumChannelContinuity.theorem_one.description: Theorem 1: for arbitrary CPTP channels between nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, regularized stabilized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence tends to regularized relative entropy as the order approaches one from either side. Values are in bits and may be infinite. No quantum bridge hypotheses remain.

QuantumChannelContinuity.blockRenyi_tend.description: For each fixed admissible Rényi order p≥1/2 with p≠1, the normalized block channel divergences converge to the supremum definition of regularized divergence, including infinite values.

QuantumChannelContinuity.blockRelative_t.description: The normalized relative-entropy block divergences converge to the supremum definition of regularized relative entropy, including infinite values.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRenyi.description: Support-aware sandwiched Rényi divergence of density states, converted from natural logarithms to bits; singular operators and infinity are handled by the underlying concrete definition.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRelative.description: Support-aware Umegaki relative entropy of density states in bits, allowing an infinite value when support inclusion fails.

QuantumChannelContinuity.channelRenyi.description: Stabilized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence: supremum over actual pure inputs on the input space together with an equally sized reference.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularizedReny.description: Supremum over positive block lengths of stabilized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence per channel use. The separate block-limit theorem identifies this supremum with the paper's limit.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularizedRela.description: Supremum over positive block lengths of stabilized relative-entropy channel divergence per channel use. The separate block-limit theorem identifies this supremum with the paper's limit.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRenyi_tend.description: Two-sided order-one limit of the actual state sandwiched Rényi divergence equals state relative entropy for arbitrary density states, including singular states and support-mismatch infinity.
The two-sided order-one state limit when the first state's support is contained in the second state's support; singular density operators are allowed.
Below-one state Rényi divergence tends to infinity at order one when support inclusion fails.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRenyi_le_o.description: Order monotonicity of sandwiched Rényi divergence for arbitrary density states: 1/2<α≤β and α,β≠1 imply Dα≤Dβ, including comparisons across one.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRenyi_mono.description: State sandwiched Rényi divergence is monotone in its order on the open interval (1/2,1), with singular states allowed.
State sandwiched Rényi divergence is monotone in its order on (1,∞), with singular states allowed.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRenyi_data.description: Data processing for the concrete support-aware state Rényi divergence at orders α≥1/2 other than one, under a CPTP map.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stateRelative_d.description: Data processing for concrete Umegaki relative entropy under a CPTP map, allowing singular states.

QuantumChannelContinuity.HockeySlackAtta.description: Intermediate proposition specifying a completely positive upper slack for N−γM whose trace effect is bounded by the stabilized hockey-stick testing optimum. It is proved for nonnegative γ by hockeySlackAttainment_of_nonneg.

QuantumChannelContinuity.hockeySlackAtta.description: For every channel pair and γ≥0, construct the exact completely positive slack bounded by the stabilized hockey-stick optimum, using Choi operators and closed-cone separation. Discharges the earlier slack-attainment hypothesis.
Specialize exact completely positive slack attainment to γ≥1, the range needed by the threshold argument.

QuantumChannelContinuity.sdpSlackCone_is.description: The finite-dimensional positive semidefinite slack cone is closed for a positive trace-preserving real linear map on Hermitian operators.

QuantumChannelContinuity.sdpSlack_separa.description: Closed-cone separation supplies a dual witness when the semidefinite slack feasibility assertion fails; used to prove exact slack attainment.

QuantumChannelContinuity.fixed_dilation_.description: Given a dilation of N and γ≥0, construct a filter in that same environment whose channel is CP-dominated by γM and whose operator-norm error is at most the square root of the stabilized hockey-stick divergence. Slack attainment is proved internally.
Intermediate filter construction taking exact CP-slack attainment as a premise; the completed wrapper fixed_dilation_hockey_filter supplies that premise.
Construct a prescribed-environment filter from a completely positive upper slack and its trace bound, with an operator-norm error controlled by the square root of that bound.

QuantumChannelContinuity.cptp_has_nontri.description: Every CPTP channel with nonzero input space has an actual Stinespring dilation in a finite nonzero environment.

QuantumChannelContinuity.stabilized_chan.description: Lift the supplied dilation-decomposition Schatten bound to arbitrary reference spaces and actual entangled inputs, for 1<p≤2. This is the one-shot stabilized estimate used near order one.

QuantumChannelContinuity.channelRenyi_di.description: For 1<p≤2, bound stabilized channel Rényi divergence using a supplied finite dilation decomposition, component operator norms, and CP domination weights.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularizedReny.description: For 1<p≤2, extend the dilation-decomposition Rényi bound to regularized channel divergence through actual tensor words and block-supremum regularization. This is a restricted version sufficient for Theorem 1, not a formalization of the paper's full α>1 decomposition lemma.
For 1<p≤2, the supplied dilation decomposition yields finiteness and the exponential regularized Schatten estimate with sum of norm/domination weights.

QuantumChannelContinuity.hockey_three_pi.description: For 1<p≤2, combine low and high hockey-stick filters into the concrete three-piece exponential bound on regularized Rényi divergence. This intermediate theorem takes a CP cap and two slack-attainment premises, all supplied in the final finite-case assembly.

QuantumChannelContinuity.wordDilation_su.description: Summing all finite tensor-word dilations reconstructs the tensor power of the supplied sum dilation, using the canonical concrete tensor-power spaces.

QuantumChannelContinuity.wordDilation_no.description: The operator norm of a tensor-word dilation is bounded by the product of its component norm bounds, including the empty word.

QuantumChannelContinuity.wordDilation_cp.description: Tensor-word dilation channels inherit product CP-domination weights against the actual channel tensor power.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularizedRela.description: Regularized relative entropy is finite exactly when N is completely positively dominated by a finite nonnegative multiple of M. Provides the finite-case CP cap without an extra channel hypothesis.

QuantumChannelContinuity.finite_cap_of_c.description: From a finite CP-domination constant, construct the cap and uniform block domination needed by the threshold proof.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularizedReny.description: At orders p>1, applying regularization to the n-fold tensor-power channels multiplies the original regularized Rényi divergence by n, for n>0.
For every p≥1/2 other than one, regularized divergence of n-fold channel powers equals n times the original regularized divergence, for n>0.

QuantumChannelContinuity.ennreal_superad.description: Extended Fekete theorem: a superadditive nonnegative extended-real sequence divided by block length converges to the supremum of its positive-length ratios, including infinity.

QuantumChannelContinuity.RemainingFinite.description: Historical finite-case interface whose fields include a raw three-piece Schatten estimate. The completed path constructs this record through QuantumThresholdInputs.toRemaining; it is not an assumption of theorem_one.

QuantumChannelContinuity.QuantumThreshol.description: Intermediate record of finite relative entropy, order monotonicity, CP caps, block slack attainment, and power scaling. The completed assembly constructs these fields from proved ingredients in the finite branch.

QuantumChannelContinuity.quantumThreshol.description: Construct every QuantumThresholdInputs field from finite regularized relative entropy and actual right-order monotonicity: CP caps, finiteness, slack attainment, and power scaling are supplied by concrete proved lemmas.

QuantumChannelContinuity.QuantumThreshol.description: Derive the precise raw estimate used in the scalar threshold argument from actual block channels, constructed Stinespring dilations, the regularized three-piece bound at 1<p≤2, and proved power scaling.
Construct the earlier RemainingFiniteInputs record, supplying its raw Schatten field from the proved three-piece estimate.

QuantumChannelContinuity.RemainingFinite.description: Construct the scalar analytical threshold record from concrete channel quantities, supplying the weak and Rényi testing bounds via proved quantum measurement bounds.

ChannelContinuity.FiniteAnalyticInputs.t.description: The scalar three-piece amplification and weak-testing argument identifies the right-order infimum threshold with relative entropy, under the explicitly listed analytical record.

ChannelContinuity.FiniteAnalyticInputs.r.description: Conclude right continuity of the scalar Rényi-rate function from the analytical threshold input record. Concrete quantum code constructs that record.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularized_rig.description: Conclude finite-case right continuity for actual regularized channel divergences from the constructed threshold record; no filter or Schatten estimate is separately assumed here.

QuantumChannelContinuity.regularizedReny.description: Left continuity of the block-input supremum follows from actual state limits and pointwise left-order monotonicity, without finite divergence being required.

QuantumChannelContinuity.theorem_one_of_.description: Prove both sides of Theorem 1 in the infinite-relative-entropy branch using an actual support-mismatch witness; no extra state/filter assumptions are needed.
Assemble finite and infinite branches of channel continuity, with only pointwise state-order monotonicity left as input. theorem_one supplies both monotonicity proofs.

QuantumChannelContinuity.inputRenyi_mono.description: Actual normalized block-output Rényi divergence is monotone on (1/2,1), inherited from the proved arbitrary-state order monotonicity.
Actual normalized block-output Rényi divergence is monotone on (1,∞), inherited from the proved arbitrary-state order monotonicity.
